title: Ranbp2 knockdown yields gated RNA/SUMO and calcium-synaptic programs rather than a uniform nuclear-pore response
exact_observed_result: Ranbp2 knockdown produced FDR-positive signatures in 6 of 20 tested cell types. 022 L5 ET CTX Glut had FDR-supported target depletion, Ranbp2 logFC -0.536 and FDR 0.00653, plus a 56-gene mixed RNA/nuclear response including Gpr162, Dync1h1, Rbm15, Kmt2a, Srrm2, and Pcbp1. 308 CB GABA instead had 98 FDR genes enriched for calcium/synaptic transcripts, including Grm1, Epha4, Itpr1, Prkcg, Kcna6, Dlg2, and Cacna2d2.
biological_interpretation: A RANBP2/SUMO nuclear-pore perturbation is read out differently by different neurons: cortical L5 ET cells couple it to RNA and nuclear-protein abundance, whereas cerebellar GABA cells expose a calcium/synaptic program.
caveats: The 155 MB Glut and 052 Pvalb GABA responses had weak or absent measured Ranbp2 transcript depletion; 14 of 20 tested classes had zero FDR-level downstream genes.

prior_expectation.summary: RANBP2 is a nuclear-envelope SUMO E3 ligase component, so RNA/nuclear-protein responses are plausible; the cerebellar calcium/synaptic arm is cell-state-specific and not a generic nuclear-pore signature.

citations.supports: RanBP2/RanGAP1*SUMO1/Ubc9 as a SUMO E3 ligase
